title: Long TBT — FOMC July 28-29 Hawkish Hold + Tariff Stagflation: September Hike at 82%
entry: $36.50–39.50 (intraday July 24). TBT is at $37.55 (July 23 close), with the 30Y at 5.188% and September hike probability at 82% — the most adverse rate-path setup since the original TBT thesis was established in July 2. This reload establishes a fresh position ahead of FOMC July 28-29 with two NEW catalysts that did not exist for the original position: (1) Trump tariffs of 10-12.5% on 99.4% of US imports took effect July 24, adding a structural August CPI inflationary input on top of the already-embedded $100 Brent oil shock; (2) FOMC July 28-29 now carries 19.4% July hike probability — the first near-20% July odds of the cycle — creating an asymmetric scenario where even a 'hawkish hold' (hold rates but explicitly signals September as live) sends TBT materially higher. Enter at market on July 24 open or on any intraday dip to $36-37. Do not initiate above $41 — at that level TBT has already priced most of the FOMC-week move and the R/R compresses for a new entry. Note: the prior TBT position (long-tbt-warsh-sintra-july-hike-2026-07-02) expires July 25; this reload is a fresh position with updated entry levels and a new catalyst framework.
stop_loss: $33.00 daily close (~12.1% below $37.55 reference) — at $33, TLT has rallied above $91, implying the 10Y has fallen below 4.15%, which would occur ONLY if: (1) FOMC July 28-29 delivers a genuine dovish surprise — not just a hold, but explicit language closing the door on September (e.g., 'the committee does not expect to raise rates in September'); (2) a macro shock (SPX -5% in a single session, VIX above 30) triggers flight-to-quality into Treasuries that overwhelms the rate-hike pricing; or (3) Trump tariffs are partially walked back via USTR blanket exemption within 10 days, removing the August CPI inflation input and collapsing September hike probability from 82% to below 40%. Below $33, the entire stagflation-hike thesis is structurally broken; exit immediately on a daily close below this level.

risk_reward: 1:4.1 to Target 3 from $37.55 reference (risk $4.55; T3 reward $18.45)
catalyst: Three simultaneous inputs on July 24 establish a materially stronger TBT thesis than existed for the prior position: (1) Trump tariffs of 10-12.5% on 99.4% of US imports (effective July 24) layer a structural August CPI inflationary input on top of the already-embedded $100 Brent energy shock — making an August CPI print above 4.5% near-mathematical unless oil reverses dramatically within 10 days; (2) FOMC July 28-29 carries 19.4% probability of a July hike — the first near-20% July hike odds in this cycle — and even a hold with explicit hawkish language on September timing would validate and extend TBT's upside; (3) the 30Y at 5.188% (breaching the 5.00% trigger for the second consecutive session) establishes a new structural anchor for long-duration rates, breaking the ceiling that had previously capped the Warsh hike thesis. TBT (ProShares UltraShort 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF) provides 2x leveraged inverse exposure to TLT; when the 10Y rises, TBT rises at approximately 2x the TLT move, making it the highest-conviction instrument for the rate-path trade with defined stop-loss exposure.
thesis:
The stagflation framework that is now operational — oil at $100 Brent (supply-side inflation from Iran/Hormuz conflict) + tariffs at 10-12.5% on 99.4% of US imports (demand-side inflation on consumer goods, electronics, food) + September rate-hike probability at 82% — is the most adverse combination for long-duration Treasury bonds since the 2022 tightening cycle. TBT is the direct expression of this framework.

The tariff catalyst is the critical new input that distinguishes this reload from the prior position. The original Warsh Sintra TBT thesis (established July 2) rested on the hawkish rate-path signal. That thesis played out partially: TBT moved from the $34.50-36.50 entry zone to $37.55 (a 5-7% gain) as September hike probability rose from 33% to 82%. What the original thesis did NOT anticipate was the Trump tariff layer arriving simultaneously with the FOMC week and Brent $100. These tariffs are not temporary commodity price shocks — they are structural policy inputs that permanently raise the price level of imported consumer goods, food, and electronics. The August CPI report (estimated release August 12) will be the first to fully capture the combined effect of Brent above $100 (embedded from the Iran conflict) AND the tariff layer. If August CPI prints at 4.7%+ (which the market currently does not fully price), September hike probability moves from 82% to 93%+, sending TBT from $37.55 toward $43 (T1).

The FOMC July 28-29 meeting itself is a binary event with an asymmetric TBT payoff. There are three scenarios. In the 80.6% probability hold-without-hawkish-language scenario, TBT stays roughly flat (+/-3%) near current levels — the tariff and oil inputs are already embedded, and a neutral FOMC changes nothing structurally. In the 19.4% probability July-hike scenario, TBT gaps +12-18% on the decision day — this is T1 territory immediately. In the most likely alternative (a 'hawkish hold' where rates are unchanged but Powell's language explicitly keeps September live with oil and tariff language), TBT moves up 6-10% toward $40-42. Two of the three scenarios are positive for TBT; only the dovish-hold scenario (which requires Powell to walk back the 19.4% July hike pricing without hawkish September language) produces a flat or slightly negative TBT outcome. This asymmetry justifies the 3% position size at medium conviction.

The 30Y at 5.188% is analytically important beyond the TBT trade. The 5% level on the 30Y was the regime trigger in the morning briefing; a second consecutive close above 5.00% signals that the long end of the curve has established a new structural floor. This is important for TBT because TBT tracks the 20+ year Treasury — its underlying bond duration is approximately 17-18 years at current yields. When the 30Y stays above 5%, TLT (TBT's inverse) faces persistent structural selling from pension funds, insurance companies, and sovereign wealth funds that have been underweight duration for 18 months and see 5%+ as a reinvestment opportunity only at lower price levels (i.e., they're NOT buying TLT, which means TLT stays down and TBT stays up). This institutional flow dynamic provides a tailwind for TBT beyond the FOMC single-event exposure.

The counter-party argues: (1) TBT has already moved from $33.49 (July 2 original entry) to $37.55 (+12%) — the Warsh/September hike thesis is already well-priced; (2) at 82% September hike probability, there is limited incremental upside from further September pricing, and the risk of a dovish surprise (whether from FOMC communication or a black-swan ceasefire in Iran) is asymmetrically negative for TBT at these levels; (3) TBT's daily reset mechanism creates volatility decay in a choppy market — holding through the FOMC event without the thesis immediately resolving generates compounding drag. These risks are managed by the 12.1% stop at $33 and the defined 4-6 week horizon.
bull_case: FOMC July 28-29 delivers a 'hawkish hold' with Powell explicitly citing 'tariff-driven goods inflation' and 'energy price pass-through' as incompatible with the 2% CPI timeline. September hike language is explicit: 'the committee will assess whether additional tightening is necessary at the September meeting.' September hike probability moves from 82% to 95% on July 29. 10Y moves from 4.71% to 4.88% on July 29 session. TBT closes July 29 at $42.50. META and MSFT report July 29 with AI capex guidance confirming Treasury supply concerns. August 12 CPI prints 4.8%. TBT reaches $49 (T2) by August 14. September 16 hike executed; TBT approaches $56 (T3) by October.
bear_case: FOMC July 28-29 is a genuine dovish hold: Powell's post-meeting statement emphasizes 'material uncertainty from tariff policy' as a reason to pause the rate path, explicitly signals that September is NOT a live meeting until August CPI is evaluated, and 10Y falls from 4.71% to 4.40% as markets price a lower-for-longer scenario. TBT falls from $37.55 to $34.50 on July 29. The $33 stop is not triggered but TBT spends 2-3 weeks in a holding pattern below the FOMC-week entry price. Iran-US diplomatic back-channel signals emerge, pushing Brent toward $88, partially deflating the August CPI inflation story. Stop maintained at $33 until August 12 CPI resolves the scenario definitively.
invalidation: $33.00 daily close (TLT rally / 10Y below 4.15% — September hike thesis structurally reset); OR FOMC July 28-29 statement explicitly closes the door on September hike ('the committee does not expect further tightening in 2026' or equivalent); OR August CPI prints below 4.0% (oil-and-tariff pass-through was less than modeled — inflation is not re-accelerating); OR Iran-US ceasefire formally agreed AND Hormuz transit resumes above 70% capacity within 10 days (removes the Brent $100 contribution to August CPI); OR 10Y falls below 4.30% for two consecutive sessions (flight-to-quality from a macro shock has overwhelmed the rate-hike framework)
